test_title: PYST 34: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 1 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

Native
solution:
The correct answer is **"Foreign".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Native"** refers to something or someone that belongs to a particular place or country, or is a characteristic or inherent quality of a person or thing.

 
 
• For example: "She is a **native **of New York" or "The **native **language of Japan is Japanese."
 
 
 
• **"Foreign" **is the **opposite **of **"native"** and refers to something or someone that comes from a different place or country.
 
 
• For example: "He speaks a **foreign **language fluently" or "The restaurant serves **foreign **cuisine."
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **"Innate"** means something that is inherent or natural, present from birth or inherent in a person or thing.

 
 
• For example: "Her **innate **talent for music was evident at a young age."
 
 
 
• **"State"** refers to a political division within a country, or can also mean the condition or quality of something.
 
 
• For example: "The **state **of California is located on the west coast of the United States" or "The **state **of the economy is concerning."
 
 
 
• **"Distant"** means something that is far away in space or time, or has a lack of closeness or intimacy.
 
 
• For example: "The nearest gas station is too **distant **to walk to" or "He has a **distant **relationship with his father."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• **'Distant' **is not an antonym of '**native**' because they are not opposites in meaning.
 
• '**Distant**' means far away or remote, while 'native' refers to something or someone that belongs to a particular place or was born in a particular place.
 
• These two words have unrelated meanings and are not opposite to each other.
